facts.claim: LEMON ListDigraph is directed.
facts.source_quote: This is the closest structural match in the evidence I examined. Its directed ListDigraph and undirected ListGraph support additions and removals, while the tutorial also describes changing endpoints and contracting or splitting graph elements. The graph concepts provide iterators and maps for attaching data. ListGraph stores linked-list relationships inside vectors and offers reservation operations, which makes it particularly relevant to the concern about excessive separate allocations. The same library exposes different tradeoffs: Smart representations provide less mutation flexibility, and StaticDigraph targets a graph built once and then traversed.

The history also contains support for power-law degree sequences, which is relevant to generating a demanding test workload, without proving that all operations handle degree skew efficiently.

2. Official self-hosted Bitwarden — https://bitwarden.com/help/hosting-faqs/
